items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the functor of points of a formal scheme satisfies the sheaf condition for fpqc coverings (statement lines 646-652). The proof reduces the topology to the case of a Zariski covering together with a covering by a single faithfully flat ring map, and uses that the sheaf condition for Zariski coverings was already observed when the functor of points was introduced (proof lines 654-660). The substance is the descent of a morphism along a faithfully flat ring map, and it is carried out in three steps. First, a morphism from the spectrum of the faithfully flat extension whose two pullbacks to the tensor square agree is shown to come from a set-theoretic map on the base, by a descent statement for maps of sets; continuity of that map is then deduced from the corresponding quotient topology statement and continuity of the given morphism (proof lines 662-671). Second, the problem is localised: an affine formal open subscheme containing the image of a chosen point is selected, a standard affine open neighbourhood of the point on which the image stays inside that subscheme is chosen, and the restriction of the morphism above it is converted into a continuous ring map into a localisation of the extension, whose two further localisations agree by hypothesis (proof lines 673-684). Third, the ring map is descended: since the localisation of the faithfully flat extension is still faithfully flat, the equalizer statement for a faithfully flat ring map identifies the fixed ring, so the ring map factors uniquely through a ring map to the localisation of the base, which has the same open kernel and hence is continuous, and therefore defines a morphism on the chosen open (proof lines 684-692). The conclusion that the local morphisms glue is left to the reader (proof lines 694-700). The claim is H2: one descent argument is carried through three stages -- set-theoretic, topological and algebraic -- and each stage is displayed, with the single omitted step being the routine glueing of morphisms that have already been constructed locally.
